## Accepted scope

Existing published results refute KP-1.64(a), the canonical induced double-contact-cover Stein-fillability implication to transverse quasipositivity. They also refute the twofold slice-Bennequin-sharpness implication in (c), and hence any blanket version of (c) allowing order two.

The positive transverse closure of b6 = (sigma1 sigma2)^6 sigma1^5 sigma2^-21 is a knot with exponent sum -4 and self-linking -7. Its canonical induced cyclic double contact branched cover is Stein fillable. A separate Hayden/generalized-Jones argument proves that its entire oriented smooth knot type is nonquasipositive. Since 2g4(K)-1 >= -1 > -7, its slice-Bennequin inequality is strictly unsharp.

Clause (b), whose hypothesis is a Stein-fillable induced cyclic cover for some n > 2, is not settled by the inspected sources or this audit. A separately restricted higher-order-only version of (c) is also not settled. This does not mark the complete three-part problem solved or assert global openness of the residual questions.

## Evidence and attribution

This theoretical edition includes the complete authored mathematical/source audit, with all mathematical sections 1–7 preserved byte-for-byte, and the separate independent AI acceptance. The full proof chain includes the original K3 clauses, the Brejevs–Wand theorem/proof, Baldwin tightness, Min–Nonino's published all-tight-structures Stein-fillability theorem in the negative-r case, the induced-contact covering identification, transverse Markov/quasipositivity transfer, explicit sharpness obstruction, and the distinct smooth-knot-type argument.

Primary published inputs include Brejevs–Wand, [*Stein-fillability and positivity in the mapping class group*](https://eprints.gla.ac.uk/348867/), JSG 24(2) (2026), 467–477; Min–Nonino, [*Tight contact structures on a family of hyperbolic L-spaces*](https://eprints.gla.ac.uk/390111/), Geometriae Dedicata 220:45 (2026); and Hayden, [*Minimal braid representatives of quasipositive links*](https://msp.org/pjm/2018/295-2/pjm-v295-n2-p09-s.pdf), Pacific J. Math. 295(2) (2018), 421–427. The complete primary citations and version/inspection limits are retained in the audit and source catalogue.

The accepted Brejevs–Wand manuscript was inspected; final JSG publisher-PDF identity is not claimed. Min–Nonino's actual published 42-page PDF is the operative dependency. Fifteen retained public PDF identities were recomputed and matched for this edition. Inspection logs refer to the original source audit, not a new reading pass during packaging.

This is existing-result verification, with zero new substantive proof-search approaches and no novelty or historical-priority claim. The reviews are AI mathematical audits, not human peer review or formal proof-assistant verification. Hashes, sizes, comparisons, and patch replay are publication-integrity checks only.

## Exact addition-only scope

Add exactly the nine files below under `unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/2723/`. The package includes the full audit, acceptance/status, clause dispositions, public source metadata/inspection history, provenance account, and noncircular manifest. Provenance-only edits are documented; the originals remain untouched.

No executable scripts, fixtures, computational result files, execution logs, copied third-party source bodies or images, dataset contents, private sources, private inventories or inventory digests, or private coordination material are included. No QUEUE.md or unrelated repository file is changed.
